mainTopic: End of the פרק on exile (rent in the ערי מקלט and returning to one's former standing) and the start of the משנה listing sins that bring מלקות
overview: This עמוד finishes the פרק about people exiled for killing by accident, then starts the פרק about מלקות. First, the משנה records two disputes between רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר. The first is whether the רוצח pays rent to the לויים in the ערי מקלט. The second is whether he gets back his old public office when he goes home. רב כהנא says the rent dispute is about the six main cities. רבא says it is about the forty-two other לויים cities. A ברייתא then shows the same two תנאים arguing about a freed עבד עברי and about the רוצח: does a returning person regain his ancestors' honored standing? After the הדרן, a new משנה lists sins that bring מלקות, including forbidden relationships and marriages, Temple and food sins, and eating טבל. רבי שמעון and the חכמים then argue over how much טבל one must eat to be liable. The גמרא notes that the list includes כרת cases but not court death-penalty cases, and it begins a ברייתא to show the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. That ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Does the exiled killer pay rent to the Levites?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה records a dispute: רבי יהודה says the killer pays rent to the לויים, and רבי מאיר says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The killers would pay rent to the לויים. This is רבי יהודה's view. רבי מאיר says they would not pay them rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks whether a person exiled to a עיר מקלט must pay rent to the לויים who own the city. רבי יהודה says yes, and רבי מאיר says no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערי מקלט were cities that belonged to the לויים. So the question is whether the killer is a paying tenant there, or whether the תורה gave him the right to live there for free.

keyTerms.meaning: Paying a fee or rent
The Levites, who owned the cities of refuge
Cities of refuge for someone who killed by accident

phrases.english: They would pay a fee to the Levites,
phrases.notes: "They" means the people who killed by accident and now live in the city of refuge.

phrases.english: the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Meir says:
They would not pay them a fee.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲלִים הָיוּ שָׂכָר לַלְוִיִּם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the רוצח pays rent to the לויים. רבי מאיר: he does not.

steps.title: Does he get back his old office when he returns home?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה records a second dispute: רבי מאיר says the killer gets back his former position of authority, and רבי יהודה says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he returns to the office he used to hold. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says he does not return to the office he used to hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the time after the killer is freed and goes home. The question is whether he takes back his old public position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice that the names have switched sides. In the rent dispute רבי יהודה was the one who said "yes." Here רבי מאיר says "yes" and רבי יהודה says "no."

keyTerms.meaning: A position of authority or public office
Returns

phrases.english: And he returns to the office that he held,
the statement of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה חוֹזֵר לִשְׂרָרָה שֶׁהָיָה בָּהּ.
phrases.english: He would not return to the office that he held.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחוֹזֵר לִשְׂרָרָה שֶׁהָיָה בָּהּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: he returns to his former office. רבי יהודה: he does not.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the argument is only about the six cities
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the rent dispute is about the six main ערי מקלט, and that both תנאים agree rent is paid in the forty-two other לויים cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The dispute is about the six cities. One Sage holds that "for you" means only for refuge. The other Sage holds that "for you" means for all your needs. But in the forty-two cities, everyone agrees they would pay rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב כהנא, who explains which cities the argument is about and why the תנאים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the six cities "for you." רבי יהודה reads this as "for you to find refuge," so the killer must still pay rent. רבי מאיר reads it as "for all your needs," which includes free housing. The forty-two cities are not described as "for you," so everyone agrees rent is paid there.

keyTerms.meaning: The six main cities of refuge
The forty-two other לויים cities, which also gave refuge
"For you," the word in the פסוק that the argument depends on
Taking someone in and giving refuge
For all your needs
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Kahana said:
The dispute is about the six cities,
for one Sage holds that "for you" means for refuge.
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:11. This one Sage is רבי יהודה, so the killer still pays rent.

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds that "for you" means for all your needs.
But in the forty-two cities,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הָיוּ מַעֲלִין לָהֶם שָׂכָר.
phrases.english: everyone agrees they would pay them rent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the rent dispute from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about the six cities and turns on how to read "לכם." In the forty-two cities everyone agrees rent is paid.

steps.title: רבא: "for you" clearly means all your needs
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב כהנא: the word "לכם" plainly means "for all your needs," so no one could read it as refuge only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But "for you" certainly means for all your needs!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the basis of רב כהנא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא needed רבי יהודה to read "לכם" as refuge only. רבא says that reading is not reasonable. The plain meaning of "for you" is full use, so רבי יהודה could not be arguing over this word.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, certainly
It means, it implies

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But "for you" certainly means for all your needs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that רבי יהודה reads "לכם" as refuge only
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of "לכם" is full use, so this word cannot be what the two תנאים argue about.

steps.title: רבא: the argument is only about the forty-two cities
steps.stepSummary: רבא moves the dispute to the forty-two cities. They argue over how far the comparison "ועליהם תתנו" goes. In the six cities, everyone agrees no rent is paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The dispute is about the forty-two cities. One Sage holds that "and beside them you shall give" makes them like the six only for refuge. The other Sage holds it makes them like the six in every way. Just as the six are for all your needs, so are these. But in the six cities, everyone agrees they would not pay rent.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב כהנא, רבא offers his own explanation. He flips which group of cities is under debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that the six cities are "for all your needs," so no rent is paid there. The forty-two cities are linked to the six by "ועליהם תתנו." רבי יהודה says the link covers only refuge, so rent is paid. רבי מאיר says the link is complete, so the forty-two are rent-free too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals a new explanation that replaces the old one
"And beside them you shall give," the פסוק that links the forty-two cities to the six
Like those (the six cities)
Just as ... so too; a comparison formula

steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא: the dispute is about the six cities, and everyone agrees rent is paid in the forty-two. רבא: the dispute is about the forty-two cities, and everyone agrees no rent is paid in the six.
steps.confusionAlert: The two אמוראים do not just disagree on details. Their "agreed" cases are opposite. Keep track of which group of cities each one says is under debate.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The dispute is about the forty-two cities,
for one Sage holds that "and beside them you shall give"
means like those, only for refuge.
And the other Sage holds that "and beside them you shall give" means like those:
just as those are for all your needs,
so too these are also for all your needs.
But in the six cities,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל לֹא הָיוּ מַעֲלִים לָהֶן שָׂכָר.
phrases.english: everyone agrees they would not pay them rent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב כהנא's explanation after the challenge in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about the forty-two cities and turns on how far the comparison "ועליהם תתנו" reaches. In the six cities no rent is paid.

steps.title: A freed Hebrew slave: does he regain his family's standing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second dispute and brings a related ברייתא about an עבד עברי. רבי יהודה says he returns to his family but not to the honored standing his ancestors held.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He returns to the office he held, etc." The Sages taught: "And he returns to his family, and to the estate of his fathers he shall return." He returns to his family, but not to what his fathers held. This is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the office dispute in the משנה. It brings a parallel ברייתא about a Hebrew slave who goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases involve a person who was away and then comes back: the slave from servitude, the killer from exile. רבי יהודה reads "his family" as the only thing he regains, and not his ancestors' position. This matches רבי יהודה's view in the משנה that the killer does not get his office back.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish servant who goes free at the end of his term or at יובל
The estate (holding) of his fathers
What his ancestors held, meaning their positions and honor
Etc.; shows that only the start of the quote is given

phrases.english: He returns to the office that he held, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the second dispute of the משנה (step 2) to show which part the גמרא is now discussing.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And he returns to his family,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:41, said about a Hebrew slave who goes free.

phrases.english: and to the estate of his fathers he shall return":
to his family he returns,
but he does not return to what his fathers held,
the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹזֵר לִשְׂרָרָה שֶׁהָיָה בָּהּ כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the office dispute from step 2 with a related ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the freed עבד עברי returns to his family but not to his ancestors' positions.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: he returns to be like his ancestors
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the freed slave also regains the standing his ancestors held. He reads "אחזת אבותיו" as "like his fathers."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: He even returns to what his fathers held. "To the estate of his fathers" means like his fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives his side of the ברייתא's dispute and his source in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads "the estate of his fathers" as more than land. It also means restoring him to his family's honored position. This fits רבי מאיר's view in the משנה that the killer returns to his former office.

keyTerms.meaning: Like his fathers, meaning with the same standing they had
He also, he even

steps.whatToRemember: Each תנא is consistent across the slave and the killer. רבי מאיר says a returning person regains his former honor. רבי יהודה says he does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא שָׁב לְמַה שֶּׁהֶחְזִיקוּ אֲבוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: He even returns to what his fathers held,
"to the estate of his fathers" means like his fathers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף הוּא שָׁב לְמַה שֶּׁהֶחְזִיקוּ אֲבוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the freed slave returns to his ancestors' standing, learned from "אל אחזת אבותיו," which means "like his fathers."

steps.title: The extra word 'he shall return' includes the killer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying the same rule applies to the exiled רוצח, learned from the extra word 'ישוב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true for someone sent into exile. When the פסוק says 'he shall return,' it comes to include the killer.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא about the עבד עברי finishes by saying the same rule also covers the רוצח who was sent to an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ישוב' in the עבד עברי's פסוק seems extra, so it is read as adding another person: the רוצח. This is still the end of the ברייתא from Steps 6-7, not a new statement by the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise; the same rule applies
Exile; here, the person exiled to an עיר מקלט
He shall return
To include; an extra word adds another case

phrases.english: And likewise with an exile,
when it says "he shall return"
phrases.notes: This is the word ישוב in the עבד עברי's פסוק (ויקרא 25:41).

phrases.english: it comes to include the killer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בַּגּוֹלָה, כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״יָשׁוּב״ – לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הָרוֹצֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא about the עבד עברי by extending its rule to the רוצח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra word 'ישוב' includes the רוצח in the rule of returning.

steps.title: What does 'likewise with an exile' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא's phrase about the exile is referring to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and likewise with an exile' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא's last line. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes from another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not clear in what way the רוצח is 'like' the עבד עברי. The גמרא wants to know exactly which rule carries over to him.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What does "and likewise with an exile" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which rule about returning applies to the רוצח, the way it applies to the עבד עברי.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the killer returns to his land but not his ancestors' standing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains: the רוצח goes back to his land, but according to רבי יהודה he does not regain his ancestors' honored standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'The killer shall return to the land of his holding.' He returns to his land, but he does not return to the standing his fathers held. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא about the רוצח that has the same dispute we saw about the עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק narrowly. It mentions only 'his land,' so the רוצח gets back his property but not the honor his family once had. This matches רבי יהודה's view about the עבד עברי in Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
His land holding
What his fathers held; the honored standing of his ancestors

phrases.english: As it was taught:
"The killer shall return to the land of his holding"
to the land of his holding he returns,
but he does not return to what his fathers held,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'likewise' refers to the same dispute about regaining ancestral standing, now applied to the רוצח. רבי יהודה says he does not regain it.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the killer regains his ancestors' standing too
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that the רוצח also regains his ancestors' standing, and he learns this from the עבד עברי through the shared word 'return.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: he also returns to the standing his fathers held. He learns 'return' and 'return' from there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר disagrees with רבי יהודה, and the גמרא explains where his view comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'return' appears both for the רוצח and for the עבד עברי. Through this גזירה שווה, רבי מאיר carries his ruling about the slave (Step 7) over to the רוצח: both get back their family's honored standing.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns / derives
'Return' and 'return'; the same word in two פסוקים
From there; here, from the עבד עברי
Learning one case from another because both use the same word

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: the רוצח and the עבד עברי go back home (to their land or family) but not to their ancestors' honored standing. רבי מאיר: both also get back their family's honored standing, learned through the word 'return' (שיבה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא שָׁב לְמַה שֶּׁהֶחְזִיקוּ אֲבוֹתָיו –
phrases.english: he also returns to what his fathers held,
he learns "return" and "return" from there.
phrases.notes: 'From there' means from the עבד עברי, whose פסוק also uses the word 'return.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף הוּא שָׁב לְמַה שֶּׁהֶחְזִיקוּ אֲבוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה and its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רוצח regains his ancestors' standing, learned by גזירה שווה from the עבד עברי.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing אלו הן הגולין
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the second פרק of מכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'אלו הן הגולין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק about people who go into exile ends here with the traditional closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the discussion of גלות, before the next topic, מלקות, begins.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; said when finishing a פרק
'These are the ones who go into exile'; the name of the פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "These are the ones who go into exile"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק on גלות is complete.

steps.title: New פרק: the list of people who receive lashes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the new פרק by listing forbidden relationships and marriages that are punished with מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the people who receive lashes. One who has relations with his sister, his father's sister, his mother's sister, his wife's sister, his brother's wife, his father's brother's wife, or a נדה. Also: a widow with a כהן גדול; a divorcée or a חלוצה with a regular כהן; a ממזרת or a נתינה with a regular Jew; and a Jewish woman with a נתין or a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה that lists people who get מלקות for breaking a תורה prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group is forbidden relationships (עריות) that carry כרת or a לאו but no court death penalty. The second group is marriages the Torah forbids only for certain people because of their status or lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who receive lashes (מַלְקוּת)
A woman in her menstrual state, forbidden until she immerses
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
A widow released from יבום through חליצה
A child born from a forbidden relationship such as incest or adultery
A descendant of the גבעונים, who may not marry into the community

steps.confusionAlert: In the second half of the list, the problem is not the relationship itself but the marriage. Each pair is forbidden only because of the specific status of the man or the woman.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: These are the ones who receive lashes:
one who has relations with his sister,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו, וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: or with his father's sister, or with his mother's sister,
or with his wife's sister,
or with his brother's wife,
or with the wife of his father's brother,
or with a menstruating woman.
a widow with a High Priest,
a divorcée or a woman released by chalitza with a regular priest,
a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman with a regular Jew,
a Jewish woman with a Gibeonite man or a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק and a new topic, מלקות, after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These forbidden relationships and forbidden marriages are punished with מלקות.

steps.title: One woman, two prohibitions: when a כהן gets two sets of lashes and when only one
steps.stepSummary: A woman who is both an אלמנה and a גרושה brings two sets of lashes on a כהן גדול who marries her. A woman who is both a גרושה and a חלוצה brings only one set on a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman is both a widow and a divorcée, a man who marries her is liable for two prohibitions. If she is both a divorcée and a חלוצה, he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how to count the lashes when one woman falls under two of the forbidden categories it just listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול is forbidden to marry an אלמנה and is also forbidden to marry a גרושה. Each is its own prohibition, so he gets two sets of lashes. For a woman who is both a גרושה and a חלוצה, the משנה says he gets only one set, so being in two categories does not always mean two punishments.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow, forbidden to a כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
A divorced woman, forbidden to every כֹּהֵן
A woman released from יִבּוּם through חֲלִיצָה, forbidden to a כֹּהֵן
Literally 'two names': two separate prohibitions, each bringing its own punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that any woman who fits two forbidden categories brings two sets of lashes. The משנה says outright that גרושה plus חלוצה brings only one.

phrases.english: A widow and a divorcée –
phrases.notes: This is one woman who was widowed, then remarried and was divorced. The case is a כהן גדול marrying her.

phrases.english: one is liable for her on account of two prohibitions.
A divorcée and a woman who underwent chalitzah –
phrases.notes: Here the case is a regular כהן marrying her.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם אַחַת בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: he is liable only on account of one alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה וּגְרוּשָׁה – חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a counting rule for the forbidden marriages listed in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלמנה plus גרושה brings two sets of lashes. גרושה plus חלוצה brings only one.

steps.title: Lashes for sins of impurity, the Temple, and forbidden sacrificial foods
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more people who get lashes: a טמא person who eats קודש or enters the מקדש, and one who eats חלב, דם, נותר, פיגול, or impure sacrificial meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: An impure person who ate holy food, one who entered the Temple while impure, and one who eats forbidden fat, blood, נותר, פיגול, or impure holy meat all get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on from forbidden marriages and starts listing other sins that bring מלקות, beginning with sins tied to the מקדש and קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new group in the list. Some sins here are about the person being טמא while touching holy things or places. Others are about the food itself being forbidden, like חלב, דם, נותר, פיגול, or sacrificial meat that became טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy food, meaning sacrificial meat
The בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, which a טָמֵא person may not enter
Certain forbidden fats of a domesticated animal
Sacrificial meat left over after the time allowed for eating it
A קָרְבָּן made invalid by a wrong intention about its time

phrases.english: The impure person who ate sacrificial food,
and one who enters the Temple impure,
and one who eats forbidden fat, or blood,
or notar, or piggul, or impure sacrificial meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of people who get lashes, now moving from forbidden marriages to Temple and food sins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sins of טומאה with קודש or the מקדש, and eating חלב, דם, נותר, פיגול, or impure sacrificial meat, bring מלקות.

steps.title: Lashes for offering outside, holiday sins, holy oil and incense, and forbidden animals
steps.stepSummary: The list continues with: offering קרבנות outside the Temple, eating חמץ on פסח, eating or working on יום הכיפורים, making or using the holy oil and incense for oneself, and eating נבילות, טריפות, שקצים and רמשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters or offers a קרבן outside, eats חמץ on פסח, eats or works on יום הכיפורים, blends the holy oil or incense, smears himself with the anointing oil, or eats carcasses, טריפות, or creatures, gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps adding to its list of sins that bring מלקות, covering several different areas of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases come from different parts of the תורה: קרבנות, holidays, holy items, and kosher food. What they share is the punishment. For some of these sins the תורה's punishment is כרת, and the משנה still lists them as bringing lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the Temple courtyard, where קָרְבָּנוֹת may not be offered
Leavened food, forbidden on פֶּסַח
The holy anointing oil made by מֹשֶׁה
The holy incense burned in the מִקְדָּשׁ
Animals that died without proper שְׁחִיטָה
Animals with a fatal defect or injury

phrases.english: And one who slaughters or offers up outside,
and one who eats leavened bread on Passover,
and one who eats and one who does work on Yom Kippur,
and one who blends the oil,
phrases.notes: This is mixing the holy anointing oil's recipe for his own ordinary use.

phrases.english: and one who blends the incense,
and one who smears himself with the anointing oil,
and one who eats carcasses and tereifot,
repugnant creatures and creeping creatures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list with more categories of sins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering outside, eating חמץ on פסח, eating or working on יום הכיפורים, misusing the holy oil or incense, and eating non-kosher animals and creatures all bring מלקות.

steps.title: Lashes for eating produce whose tithes or redemption were not handled
steps.stepSummary: Eating טבל, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken, or מעשר שני and הקדש that were not redeemed brings lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who ate untithed produce, or first tithe whose תרומה was not separated, or second tithe or consecrated food that was not redeemed, gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends this part of the list with sins of eating produce that still has holy portions or holiness attached to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each of these cases, a required step was skipped. Either the gifts were not separated, as with טבל and מעשר ראשון, or the food was not redeemed, as with מעשר שני and הקדש. Eating it in that state brings מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תְּרוּמוֹת and tithes have not yet been separated
The first tithe, given to the לֵוִי
The holy portion given to the כֹּהֵן
The second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
Property consecrated to the מִקְדָּשׁ

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list of sins that bring מלקות covers forbidden marriages, Temple and impurity sins, forbidden foods, holiday sins, holy oil and incense, and produce eaten before its gifts were separated or before it was redeemed.

phrases.english: He ate untithed produce,
or first tithe whose teruma was not taken,
or second tithe and consecrated property that were not redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל טֶבֶל וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְּרוּמָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with sins of eating produce before its gifts were separated or before it was redeemed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating טבל, מעשר ראשון without its תרומה, or unredeemed מעשר שני or הקדש brings מלקות.

steps.title: How much טבל must one eat to be liable?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks the minimum amount of טבל that brings מלקות. רבי שמעון says any amount, and the חכמים say a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much must a person eat from טבל to be liable? רבי שמעון says: any amount at all. The חכמים say: a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a new question about the טבל case from the last step: what is the smallest amount that brings מלקות? Two opinions are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים use the usual minimum for 'eating', which is a כזית. רבי שמעון holds that even a tiny amount makes one liable. The rest of the משנה is the debate between them.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been taken
Any amount at all, even the tiniest bit
An olive-sized amount, the standard minimum for 'eating'
Liable, here meaning liable to מלקות

phrases.english: How much must one eat from טבל
and be liable?
Rabbi Shimon says: any amount.
And the Rabbis say: an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה יֹאכַל מִן הַטֶּבֶל וִיהֵא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the minimum amount to the טבל case listed in step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: any amount of טבל makes one liable. חכמים: only a כזית.

steps.title: רבי שמעון challenges from eating an ant
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון points out that the חכמים agree one who eats an ant of any size is liable, so why require a כזית for טבל?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to them: Don't you agree with me that someone who eats an ant of any size is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון pushes back against the חכמים. He uses a case they already agree with: eating even a tiny ant brings מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a tiny ant is enough for liability, then a כזית is not always the minimum. רבי שמעון wants to apply the same idea to טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Agree, concede
Ant, one of the forbidden crawling creatures

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to them:
Do you not agree with me
regarding one who eats an ant of any size
that he is liable?
phrases.notes: An ant is one of the forbidden creeping creatures (שקצים ורמשים) that step 16 listed among the cases that bring lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the חכמים's כזית requirement from step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's view that a כזית is needed for liability
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים agree that a tiny ant brings liability, so a כזית is not a fixed minimum.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: an ant is a whole creature
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים explain that the ant is different because it is eaten whole, in its complete created form.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That is because it is in its complete created form.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי שמעון. They explain why the ant is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole creature counts as a complete forbidden item, whatever its size. Ordinary food like טבל has no such 'whole item' status, so the normal כזית minimum still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: In its complete created form, whole and intact
Because

phrases.english: They said to him:
Because it is in the form of its creation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's challenge in step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ant case shows that any amount is enough for every forbidden food.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ant brings liability only because it is a whole creature. Normal food still needs a כזית.

steps.title: רבי שמעון replies: a wheat kernel is also whole
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that a single kernel of wheat is also in its complete created form, so the same logic should apply to טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: One kernel of wheat is also in its complete created form.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון rejects the חכמים's distinction. He turns their own reason back on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being whole is what makes an ant count at any size, then a whole wheat kernel of טבל should count too. The משנה ends here without a reply from the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A kernel of wheat
Also, even

phrases.english: He said to them:
One wheat kernel is also in the form of its creation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the חכמים's answer in step 20
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'whole creature' distinction offered by the חכמים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being whole is not unique to living creatures. A single wheat kernel is also whole.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: any amount of טבל brings מלקות. חכמים: a כזית is needed, and an ant is an exception because it is a whole creature.

steps.title: The משנה lists כרת cases but not court death penalties
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the משנה includes sins punished with כרת in its list of מלקות cases, but leaves out sins punished with court-imposed death.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches people liable to כרת, but it does not teach people liable to court-imposed death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by pointing out a pattern in the משנה's list. It is setting up the next move: whose opinion does this pattern follow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many cases in the משנה carry כרת as well as a לאו, and they still get מלקות. Sins punished by בית דין with death are missing. This suggests the משנה holds that such sins never get מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: People who committed sins punished with כרת, being cut off by Heaven
People who committed sins punished with death by the court
The משנה teaches, lists

phrases.english: GEMARA: It teaches those liable to כרת,
those liable to court-imposed death
it does not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with an observation about the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's list of מלקות cases includes כרת cases but not court death-penalty cases.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows and answers that it is רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה? It is רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנא whose view matches the pattern it just noticed: רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern in step 22 depends on a מחלוקת among the תנאים. By naming רבי עקיבא, the גמרא tells us the משנה takes one side of that argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Whose opinion is it?

phrases.english: Whose is our משנה?
It is Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the pattern noticed in step 22 by naming its author
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that only כרת cases, and not court death-penalty cases, get מלקות

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: כרת cases and death-penalty cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that shows a מחלוקת about whether those liable to כרת and those liable to court death get מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Both those liable to כרת and those liable to court-imposed death...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins bringing its source for saying the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. The quote continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens with a view that treats כרת cases and death-penalty cases the same way. Once the full מחלוקת is quoted, רבי עקיבא's view will match our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that, treated the same

phrases.english: As it is taught:
Both those liable to כרת
and those liable to court-imposed death
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet; the ruling comes on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא אֶחָד חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת וְאֶחָד חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 23
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a תנאים dispute about מלקות for כרת cases and court death-penalty cases
